question: How much does it cost in the UK to implement Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central?
answer: The cost of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central implementation in the UK depends on your business requirements, number of users (see Business Central pricing and licensing), data migration needs, integrations, customisations and training requirements. A simple implementation will generally require less investment than a more complex, multi-company implementation. Dynamics Square UK can assess your requirements (or try our ERP implementation cost calculator) and provide you with a customised estimate for implementation.

question: What is the time frame for a Business Central implementation?
answer: The time required for a Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central implementation varies depending on the size and complexity of the project, and can take several weeks to several months. Factors such as data migration, integrations, customisations, testing and user training are all factors that impact the timeline. Having a defined implementation methodology and plan will help set realistic milestones and get your team ready for go-live.

question: What are the services that are included in Business Central implementation?
answer: Business Central implementation services typically include requirements analysis, solution design, system configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, user training and go-live support. This will depend on the type of business processes, existing systems and reporting requirements. Dynamics Square UK can help you create an implementation plan that aligns with your operational priorities.

question: Is it possible to move from Sage, QuickBooks or Excel to Business Central?
answer: Yes. Relevant financial and operational data can be moved from systems like Sage, QuickBooks and Excel to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. The migration process includes checking the existing data, deduplicating data, mapping and validating the migrated data. The approach will depend on the source system and the quality of data and historical records that need to be retained.

question: Is it possible to integrate Business Central with current business applications?
answer: Yes. Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central can integrate with third-party applications and Microsoft services such as Dynamics 365 Sales, Microsoft 365 and Power BI. Depending on the requirements, financial data, customer data, reporting and operational workflows can be integrated. The approach and expense of integration will depend on the applications and complexity of the data exchange.

question: Is Business Central customisable to fit my business needs?
answer: Yes. Business Central is available for configuration, extensions and integrations to meet specific business needs. An implementation partner can find out if the standard functionality meets your needs before recommending custom development. Standard features should be considered as the main features if possible, so that the cost is reduced and future changes are easier.

question: What support and training is offered after Business Central is implemented?
answer: Post implementation training enables employees to grasp the features and workflows that are relevant to their roles. Continuous Business Central support can be used to address technical issues, answer user questions, maintain integrations and address evolving business needs. Prior to go-live, it is important to have your support arrangements agreed with you so that you know who will be responsible for what and what you can expect from them.

question: How do I know if a Business Central implementation partner in the UK is right for me?
answer: Choose a Business Central implementation partner with the Microsoft Dynamics 365 experience, proven delivery method and experience with businesses similar to yours (review their case studies). Assess its data migration, integrations, testing, training, project management and post-go-live support. It is also important to have clear scope, transparent pricing and defined responsibilities when evaluating an implementation proposal.

question: Is it possible to implement Business Central in phases?
answer: Yes. Business Central can be implemented in phases, either by implementing core functionality first, and then modules, integrations or business processes. This can assist organisations to prioritise their needs, manage change and distribute implementation activities across time. The project plan should include the dependencies, testing requirements and acceptance criteria for each phase of the project.

question: Can Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central be used for manufacturing and distribution companies?
answer: Yes. Business Central offers financial management, inventory, purchasing and sales and supply chain capabilities. It also has manufacturing and service management capabilities as part of its Premium licence. The suitability will be based on the complexity of production, distribution and warehouse processes, planning requirements, and any specific functionality and integrations the business needs.
